## [0.0.8] - 2026-11-20

### Changed

- **This is a standalone-only build: `package.json` declares no `sources`, and `metaview.conversations` is not
  advertised or available.** Memory, Artifacts and Jelly see no source to bind or collect, so this build makes no
  collection, identity or Metaview call for one.
- The collection-only runtime, its registrations, default rules, conformance report and tests are removed. There are no
  `events_list` or `probe` compatibility stubs: neither is in `describe` or any method list, and an old script's call
  fails as an unknown RPC method before any Metaview or identity read. Old collection callers have no supported
  replacement in this standalone build; ordinary explicit native searches remain available but are not a migration
  path and do not inherit the collection's identity, cursor, metadata or privacy guarantees.
- Older pinned installs are unchanged, and data already collected by a consumer is not deleted or reset by this build.
- Native Metaview tools, the general tools RPC, permissions for the tools that remain, the supported host range,
  credential handling and the version are unchanged. No conformance report is generated or attached; the release
  workflow's source gate reads `sources: false`.

### Known limits

- **No conversations source or collection methods in this build.** `package.json` declares no `sources`, so Memory,
  Artifacts and other consumers cannot bind or collect Metaview conversations from this build. `events_list` and
  `probe` are not registered methods: they are absent from `describe`, and an old call fails as an unknown RPC method
  before any Metaview or identity read. An old collection caller has no supported replacement here; ordinary explicit
  native searches do not inherit the collection's identity, cursor, metadata or privacy guarantees. Older pinned
  installs remain unchanged, and already collected data is not deleted or reset by this build.
- **Some changes reach people.** A screening or sequence message, an application-review decision that can reject a candidate and sync to your ATS, and feedback to the Metaview team (a hiring decision can email the candidate) all reach people or systems outside OpenCode. At the default `access`, an agent can make them without a prompt.
- **Metaview's server decides the tools.** The plugin classifies the tools it knows. A tool Metaview adds later is not classed by the plugin: the `access` option decides whether it runs, asks or is denied, and `/metaview-status` counts it as unknown.
- **Role and plan limits.** What you can read follows your Metaview role, and reports, AI fields and full transcripts may need a paid plan. The plugin does not change either.
- **No retries.** The plugin does not retry a failed call. The error names the next step.
- **Hosts and platforms.** The plugin is tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7, 2.3.0, 2.3.1 and 2.3.2, and runs on macOS or Linux. A later 2.2 or 2.3 release starts and is reported as untested.
- **Jelly's settings need a recent Jelly.** The `jelly` settings declare their choices, which a Jelly without app#1301
  does not read: it refuses the plugin's declaration.
- Updates are not automatic for a Git install, and `opencode plugin update` and `opencode plugin check` do not work on one: to move to a newer release, remove the old entry and add the new tag.

## [0.0.7] - 2026-11-20

### Changed

- `events_list` is a tools RPC method only, like `probe`, and is no longer a tool in the `metaview` namespace or a
  `jelly.tools` entry. Memory still collects through `metaview.workspace.tools/events_list`. The default rule
  `metaview_events_list` is unchanged.
- `scripts/check-copies.mjs` no longer names a copied `src/host/tools-rpc.ts`: the tools RPC is the source contract's
  module, bundled into `dist/index.js`.
- The `@we-the-rebel-alliance/source-contract` dev dependency is v0.3.0 (it was v0.2.0): `package.json` and the
  lockfile, and the conformance test states why each v0.3 check that does not apply to this source is skipped. The
  plugin sends no new key, and its pages, methods and descriptor are unchanged.

### Known limits

- **The conversations source lists by start time.** Metaview's search orders and filters conversations by their start
  only, with no time Metaview received them, and an uploaded recording is listed at the start its uploader gave.
  - **Late arrivals:** one that appears after the source read past its start (an upload, a conversation shared with you
    later) is listed once if it started within 7 days of the cursor; one later than that is not listed, and no gap says so.
  - **Busy accounts:** the cursor de-duplicates about 200 conversations (about 28 a day over the 7 days). With more,
    the lookback is shorter, and a `window-truncated` gap says so once per shortening. A de-dup key is 25 bits of a
    hash of the id, so about 1 late arrival in 168,000 can be taken for one already listed and not listed.
  - **Retention:** the source vouches for the last 30 days, since Metaview's retention is your organization's own
    setting and no tool names it. A workspace retention shorter than 30 days can delete recordings before the source
    reads them, with no gap.
  - **Deleted or no longer yours:** one deleted, or that you lose access to (unshared, or hidden by a role change),
    before a read reaches it is not listed and is not a gap; one already listed is not retracted.
- **Some changes reach people.** A screening or sequence message, an application-review decision that can reject a candidate and sync to your ATS, and feedback to the Metaview team (a hiring decision can email the candidate) all reach people or systems outside OpenCode. At the default `access`, an agent can make them without a prompt.
- **Metaview's server decides the tools.** The plugin classifies the tools it knows. A tool Metaview adds later is not classed by the plugin: the `access` option decides whether it runs, asks or is denied, and `/metaview-status` counts it as unknown.
- **Role and plan limits.** What you can read follows your Metaview role, and reports, AI fields and full transcripts may need a paid plan. The plugin does not change either.
- **No retries.** The plugin does not retry a failed call. The error names the next step.
- **Hosts and platforms.** The plugin is tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7, 2.3.0, 2.3.1 and 2.3.2, and runs on macOS or Linux. A later 2.2 or 2.3 release starts and is reported as untested.
- **Jelly's settings need a recent Jelly.** The `jelly` settings declare their choices, which a Jelly without app#1301
  does not read: it refuses the plugin's declaration.
- Updates are not automatic for a Git install, and `opencode plugin update` and `opencode plugin check` do not work on one: to move to a newer release, remove the old entry and add the new tag.

## [0.0.5] - 2026-11-17

### Added

- **A shared-data source, `metaview.conversations`** ([#21](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/opencode-metaview/issues/21)):
  `package.json` declares source-contract `sources` (contract version 1), so Memory, Artifacts and other consumers can
  read Metaview's recorded conversations as events through the shared contract. `events_list` (a tool in the `metaview`
  namespace and a tools RPC method) lists them oldest first, once they started 3 hours ago, from
  `search_conversations`, with a cursor bound to the plugin, the source and the account; `probe` names the signed-in
  account from `get_user_context`. Metaview's retention is each organization's own setting, so the source vouches for
  the last 30 days: an older cursor or `since` answers a `gap` once per read and reads on from the window's edge. A
  conversation Metaview adds behind the cursor within 7 days of it, such as an upload listed at its call's start, is
  listed once, by a 25-bit key of its id that the cursor keeps in a Golomb-Rice coded set (about 200 fit; with more,
  a `window-truncated` gap says once per shortening that the lookback is shorter; a late arrival is taken for a listed
  one about once in 168,000). A burst sharing one start is walked by id; an answer the plugin cannot read
  fails the call and holds the cursor; a title's email addresses and phone numbers are masked, and an actor's id is a
  Metaview participant id or nothing. Each event carries metadata only: the id, start, title, link, conversation type, and
  the candidates and interviewers by name. No transcript, note, score, feedback or contact detail, and `text` is
  always empty. Both are reads, allowed by the default rules like Metaview's reads; `jelly.tools` declares
  `metaview.events_list`. `npm run conformance` runs the contract's conformance kit on fixtures and writes
  `reports/conformance-report.json`, which a release attaches.

### Changed

- The tools RPC is the source contract's `tools-rpc` module, bundled into `dist/index.js`, in place of the plugin's own
  copy of the shared module. Its methods, classes, codes and next steps are unchanged.
